subject: Offer tier consistency check — senior runtime band vs. market
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Aug 2029 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Offer tier consistency check — senior runtime band vs. market

Hi Kim & Marcus —

Following the loop with TalentBridge and final onsite debrief, we're ready to extend an offer to Daniel Singh for the Senior Runtime Engineer role (Req 4521). Comp packet below deviates from the published L6 band by +8% base to hit market midpoint for low-latency inference experience.

Quick summary:
- Title: Senior Runtime Engineer (L6)
- Proposed base: $215,000 (current L6 midpoint: $199,000)
- Equity: 0.40% 4y
- Sign-on: $25k (one-time)
- Total comp competitiveness rationale: strong kernel/quantization experience, shipping inference in prod at scale, and risk of losing to two competing offers.

Attached: Senior_Runtime_Offer_Proposal.pdf and our Comp_Band_Table_Q3_2029.xlsx with market comps highlighted.

Request: approval for an exception to the L6 base midpoint to authorize the proposed base and sign-on. If approved, I'll coordinate with Sarah (TalentBridge) and Laura in People to draft the offer.

If you need the scorecard or loop notes, I can paste them.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Martinez
Hiring Manager, Runtime Platform
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Offer tier consistency check — senior runtime band vs. market

Thanks Alex — I reviewed the attachment and comp table. Short note from Compensation:

- We generally avoid stretching the published band more than ±5% without exec sign-off.
- The market data supports a premium for low-latency inference specialists in this geo, and the candidate’s non-compete window is short which reduces long-term retention risk.
- If you want to award +8% base at L6, we need a documented business justification and an approval note from Marcus. Also a brief retention plan (milestones for second-year uplift or performance-based vesting acceleration).

I can prepare the comp exception memo; please add the key reasons I should include (impact metrics, ramp expectations).

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Compensation & Rewards
Redwood Inference

Looping in a hiring play perspective — I support the exception given the time-to-fill risk and the delivery plan Alex outlined during debrief. A couple of asks for the memo:

- Include the immediate deliverables inside 90 days (KV cache improvements, 95th percentile latency target for current model serving stack).
- Add a clear retention trigger: additional 0.05% after hitting 12-month performance milestone.
- Document candidate counter-offer window — Sarah confirmed verbal interest from two other companies and an in-flight process with one FAANG.

I’ll draft suggested bullets for the justification — aiming to keep the exception narrowly scoped and tied to measurable outcomes.

1) A short comp-exception memo from Kim capturing rationale and retention triggers.
2) A commitment from Alex for a 12-month delivery plan with measurable KPIs (90-day milestones + 12-month retention trigger).
3) Laura to confirm budget reallocation and sign-off on offer letter language for sign-on payment logistics.

Alex — please proceed to get the memo from Kim and have Laura confirm the payroll treatment. Once those are in place, Marcus approves.
